primary.title: The Iliad
primary.author: Homer
primary.rationale: The foundational epic poem of ancient Greek literature, attributed to Homer. It is a cornerstone of Western literature and widely available.

primary.title: The Odyssey
primary.author: Homer
primary.rationale: Another major epic poem attributed to Homer, detailing the journey of Odysseus. It is as fundamental as the Iliad and also widely accessible.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Homer
secondary.author: I. Morris and B. Powell
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Homeric studies, including textual criticism, archaeology, and reception.

secondary.title: Homer: The Story of the Iliad
secondary.author: Elizabeth Cook
secondary.rationale: An accessible yet scholarly introduction to the Iliad, exploring its themes, characters, and historical context.

secondary.title: The Making of Homeric Verse: The Early Greek Poets and Their Oral Art
secondary.author: G. Nagy
secondary.rationale: A seminal work that explores the oral tradition behind the Homeric epics, arguing for their composition through a long process of oral performance.

suggestions.notes: Homer's primary works are ancient epic poems. Scholarly research often focuses on their authorship, historical context, and oral tradition. The exact dates of composition are debated but are generally placed in the Archaic period.
